text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SEV P1 — GPU capacity exhaustion detected in us-west-2 (cluster inference-prod-gpu). Autoscaler attempted scale but hit max_nodes=48. Queue growth observed. Incident created.

alex: Acknowledging. I'm on call. Looking at the autoscaler logs now.

maria: seeing lots of 429s from the router to the runtime since 08:34 UTC. Customers on Dedicated experiencing throttling.

oncall-ml: queue length spike: 08:34 -> 2500 pending, 08:40 -> 4200 pending. Avg wait > 12s and climbing. Worker utilization shows many small free MIG slices (~0.5 - 1 GPU worth) that are unallocatable due to placement binpack.

alex: can you paste the autoscaler error? I'm guessing failed to provision because of AZ fragmentation, or hitting vCPU limits on nodes.

maria: paste from infra-autoscaler.log:

```
2026-03-14T08:36:12Z ERROR scale_up: reached max_nodes (48) while desired_nodes=62, reason=quota_or_limit
2026-03-14T08:36:12Z WARN placement: failed to find contiguous GPU for shard, stranded_mig_count=18
```

sanjay: confirmed: cloud quotas for us-west-2 account are at 50 total GPUs; we already have reserved capacity for Dedicated customers that pins 20 GPUs. Autoscaler wanted to go to 62 but blocked.

kevin: so we have two problems: (1) autoscaler blocked by account quotas / infra limits, (2) scheduler can't pack around small MIG sizes, leaving stranded capacity even inside existing nodes.

elaine: customer's support ticket noise increasing. CS reporting timeouts for two high-value customers (acct A & B). We need immediate mitigation and customer-facing note. @maria can you escalate to CS and draft a short status update? Mention mitigation in progress.

maria: already on it. Drafting: "We’re experiencing increased latency and intermittent throttling for model inference in us-west-2. Our engineering team is actively scaling and applying mitigations. We’ll update in 30 minutes." Thoughts?

alex: good. Start with that.

oncall-ml: live metrics:
- provisioned_nodes: 48 (max)
- total_gpus: 192 (some split into MIG partitions)
- allocated_gpus: 170
- stranded_mig_islands: 18 (sum ~5.6 GPUs unusable)
- avg_queue_latency: 14.2s
- 429_rate: 12% for last 10m

sanjay: mitigation plan (quick list):
1) Temporarily raise cloud quota request (slow — takes hours). Not useful for immediate.
2) Emergency: bump cluster max_nodes to 60 via infra admin (if quota permits). But I think quota is the blocker.
3) Runtime-level: evict low-priority batch jobs and move them to cpu-only pool. Free up GPUs.
4) Scheduler-level: run a defragmentation job — consolidate pods to free whole GPUs (evict and reschedule) — risk of transient latency.
5) Apply temporary model throttling/rate-limits per-tenant to protect HA customers.

alex: implement 3 and 5 immediately. We can do 4 if 3 isn't enough. 2 is blocked by quota but I can open an emergency support case.

kevin: I can push a job to the scheduler to mark certain MIG partitions as reclaimable and force binpack. Will take ~3-6m to run.

oncall-ml: starting eviction: targeting non-sla batch jobs labelled `batch:low-prio`. Command:

```
kubectl get pods -l batch=low-prio -n inference | xargs -n1 kubectl delete pod -n inference --grace-period=0 --force
```

alex: please do a dry-run first list so we don't kill anything customer-facing.

kevin: dry-run listed 42 pods on gpu nodes flagged batch=low-prio. Proceeding with eviction now in 2 batches to avoid thundering herd.

maria: CS update sent. Mentioned affected regions and mitigation steps.

incident-bot: NOTE: autoscaler still reporting desired_nodes=62 but blocked by quota. ticket-cloud-quota-894 opened.

oncall-ml: after first eviction batch:
- freed_gpus: 6
- stranded_mig_islands reduced to 15
- queue length down to 3200
- 429_rate down to 9%

alex: good. Keep evicting second batch, then run the defrag job if needed.

kevin: second batch done. freed_gpus total now 12. But scheduler still can't allocate for some small models because MIG shard sizes mismatch (we have many 1g.5 and 2g.5 partitions).

sanjay: can we temporarily fallback those tenants to a compatible model variant that fits into available MIG shapes? For example smaller-seq variant.

alex: yes. Run a routing rule: if model in group X then route to variant x-small (cpu fallback acceptable for low-prio, but not for acct A/B). We'll only apply to non-enterprise tenants.

maria: CS wants us to prioritize acct A/B — which models are they hitting? They're on `gpt-embed-v1` and `redwood-chat-xl`.

oncall-ml: acct A is running `redwood-chat-xl` heavy traffic. We should not throttle them lightly. Proposal: reserve 8 GPUs for high-tier dedicated tenants by preempting flexible capacity and pinning.

kevin: reserving now by applying node taints and scheduler affinity for pods with `tier=dedicated`. That will reduce general availability but protect SLAs.

alex: do it. Also enable request-level rate-limits: per-api-key token bucket at 1.5x normal and enforce 503 after burst to protect system.

maria: notifying customers of rate-limit changes.

incident-bot: action_log: eviction(batch low-prio) x2; routing-rule applied for non-enterprise -> x-small variants; node-taint applied for dedicated tier; cloud-quota ticket opened.

oncall-ml: metrics after actions (09:05 UTC):
- queue length: 800
- avg latency: 6.8s
- 429_rate: 2.3%
- reserved_for_dedicated: 8 GPUs
- stranded_mig_islands: 9 (~2.8 GPUs unusable)

alex: still some stranded capacity. We need follow-up: schedule a planned maintenance to run a full defrag that will migrate pods and re-provision nodes with uniform MIG sizing. Document risk and customer communication.

sanjay: agreed. Follow-up tasks:
- infra: request temporary quota bump and schedule node reimage (MIG standardization) — owner: sanjay
- scheduler: implement smarter binpack heuristics to prefer consolidation over spread — owner: kevin
- runtime: improve eviction policy to prefer batch gpu pods — owner: alex
- cs: send detailed RCA to affected customers in 24h — owner: maria

kevin: I'll open PR for binpack heuristics and a pilot job to run nightly defrags during low-traffic windows.

maria: handoff: I'm going offline in 30m. Who will own incident until resolution? alex?

alex: I'll be primary until 11:00 UTC. @kevin you'll handle scheduler follow-ups; @sanjay will handle infra quota/region work; @maria will drive customer comms.

incident-bot: incident status: mitigated (P1 -> P2). System load reduced, key customers protected. Please continue monitoring.

maria: thanks team. Will collate notes and prepare incident timeline. Need to make a postmortem with root cause: MIG fragmentation + quota limits + autoscaler configuration. Outline incoming.

sanjay: note for postmortem — consider adding soft eviction priorities at cloud provider level to reclaim underused MIG partitions faster.

alex: will follow up with runbook updates: add emergency steps (evict low-prio, apply routing rule, reserve GPUs for dedicated) and a checklist for opening quota escalations.

kevin: adding observability: track stranded_mig_islands metric and auto-alert threshold at >5 islands.

oncall-ml: handing off to next on-call: @kevin now. I'll remain available for questions. Good job everyone.
